# Your Working Day
## What the Company needs from you Most of your time will be spent identifying unknown chemicals, working out what they do, and turning that knowledge into something the Company can use. Every finding you record earns the site money, and good findings earn a lot of it.
The Company's research equipment is supplied through the corporate ASRS: - The [bold]XRF scanner[/bold] analyses unknown samples and identifies what's in them. - The [bold]research data terminal[/bold] stores your reports, tracks the lab's research points and offers chemical contracts from Company clients. - The [bold]synthesis simulator[/bold] lets you test new compounds before you make them for real.
The research section of the guidebook explains each machine in detail.
## The research licence All Company research on a colony depends on the colony's research licence. If the colony revokes it, the lab can keep working, but nothing it produces earns the Company a credit. Losing the licence costs the Company a great deal, so please don't give the colony a reason to take it away. If you hear that the licence is at risk, tell the Lead Researcher straight away.
## Recording your work - Write everything down. A result that isn't recorded may as well not exist. - Save your reports to the research data terminal, not to personal notes. - Label every sample with what it is, where it came from and who handled it. - Never take samples, reports or data out of the lab without the Lead Researcher's permission.
## Contracts Company clients sometimes ask the lab to supply particular chemicals. Contracts are accepted at the research data terminal and pay well when they're delivered on time. Check with the Lead Researcher before taking one on.
